svg.text: F Sub-mechanisms (2) — cutting and peeling
Each panel loops on its own. Hold the piece by physics, or weaken the skin before removing it.
source: F-first-principles.md section 6
S6/S7 grid dicing: see F-saeule; S27: see F-trommel
S38 Mini band knife
Bread, tomatoes, cooked roast, tempered meat, cake: one slice at a
time. Wheels outside the food zone; band wiped on every turn.
Feasibility H technically, M for hygiene of guides; guarding
S9 Broach-peeling
A grid whose outer cells lead to waste: only the inner sticks are kept;
first and last slices are diverted. No peeler at all.
Feasibility H to build, L on yield (55–70 % < 75 %)
S8 Heel pig

g.text: or a raw potato slice, or an ice puck

svg.text: The last food in the grid is pushed through by a follower before
washing; the vessel is swapped for the waste chute first.
Feasibility M
S26 Wheel orienter + corer

g.text: spun on an off-centre wheel: settles stem-down
axial tube punch removes the core

svg.text: A round fruit settles with its stem cavity on the wheel (apple-processing
practice); then the punch cores it and the wedge die segments it.
Feasibility M
S11 Hydro-peel for onions
Tumbled in a perforated basket under tangential water jets;
skins flush to the strainer. No compressor.
Feasibility M–L: plausible, unproven
S12 Rubber-finger skin slipper
Poultry-plucker principle: steamed potatoes, blanched tomatoes,
onions, almonds, boiled eggs lose their skins in 30–60 s.
Feasibility M
